question: By this lane: the probability that the R(3,10) lane of cert-machine decides, by 30 June 2027, whether a (3,10;40)-graph exists, either way, to the lane's certification standard.

brief.text:
# Forecast brief (the same text for each model; each answers alone, without seeing the other's answer) Question: what is the probability that the R(3,10) lane of cert-machine DECIDES, by 30 June 2027 (23:59 UTC), whether a (3,10;40)-graph exists — either way: a certified construction of one (R(3,10) ≥ 41), or a certified proof that none exists (R(3,10) ≤ 40, so R(3,10) = 40 given the known lower bound) — with the certification standard the lane uses (exact checks, LRAT through two checkers or a kernel-checked proof, premises listed)? Read the lane's public records: ~/Projects/cert-machine/corpus/r310-live/ (cases.json, boxes.json, process.json, paths.json, corrections.json, machine.json) and the published sources in corpus/r310-live/sources/ (the round ledger round1/LEDGER.md, round5/PATHS.md, the gate files). The page is https://carlostoledo.co/r310/ (do not fetch it; the records are the same). Also use what you know of the literature (Goedgebeur–Radziszowski 2013, Angeltveit's 2024–25 work and any later bound you know of, the history of R(3,k) computations) and of the lane's resources (one person with AI agents, a laptop and rented CPU pods at about US$1–3 an hour). DO NOT read: corpus/r310-live/fieldmap.json's forecast entries, the Field Map's "bets" section, or any file under notes/forecasts-2026-11-26/ other than this brief and your own folder. Answer independently. Answer in this exact form (plain text, under 350 words in all): RANGE: %–% (your 80% credible interval for the probability) POINT:

% DIRECTION: if decided, which way you expect and how strongly (e.g. "none exists, ~80%") BASIS: 4–6 short lines — what in the records moves you most, what the main risks are, what base rates you used WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: 2–3 short lines Say plainly that this is a model's forecast and not a commitment.

models.text:
Written: Thu Nov 26 01:17:34 UTC 2026 (date -u)
Claude Opus 5.5, alone. This is a model's forecast, not a commitment.

RANGE: 1%–9%
POINT: 3%
DIRECTION: none exists, ~70% (if decided)

BASIS:
- Records: three pieces closed (C35, R(7) recomputed, R(6) three-edge branch). Still open: 236 near-regular distributions, R(6) with 4–9 cross-edges (a pilot only), R(3)–R(5) (c* = 4: 60 of 69 profiles open; c* = 3: 0 of 7 closed).
- Moves me most: 20 dead paths and 32 FAIL gates. Every global route that got a price is above about 60,000–70,000 CPU-h (F1, F3), and F1's open count stayed flat. That is a lower bound, not a quote. At about US$0.03 per core-hour it could be paid for, but nothing shows the work converges.
- Base rates: R(3,9) took 1966–1982; R(3,10) has been open since 1989. The upper bound went 42 (2013) → 41 (Angeltveit 2024–25), years per step. Excluding 40 is the larger space. Several AI-assisted groups are closing slices; none is near done.
- Building one: extensions of 39-vertex graphs (37M, 43M, 18.4M) found nothing, nor did AlphaEvolve or lane 41. The best misses still have 23–24 independent 10-sets, or one triangle. This favours "none exists" and makes finding one unlikely.
- Risks: one operator who parks lanes, seven months, and much of the rigour still to build (prose reductions; Chen's unchecked 97/88 floors). The point includes ~1% for the lane re-certifying someone else's decisive proof.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT:
- Up: a whole stratum (all of c* = 4, or the 236 distributions) closed at a measured, falling cost; or a published outside proof of R(3,10) = 40 that the lane could re-check.
- Up, sharply: any (3,10;40)-graph found (checked in seconds).
- Down: the lane parked, or F1's cost turning out unbounded on the strata still open.

This is a model's forecast, not a commitment.

models.name: GPT-6.2 (Astra)
models.how: a fresh Codex session, alone, reading the brief and the records
basis: The lane certified all 977,008 configurations of the regular codegree-seven case with two LRAT checkers: it can certify a small enough reduction.
The hard cases set the date: none of ten benchmark boards closed in two CPU-hours; 236 of 519 degree distributions remain.
Angeltveit's ≤ 41 took about three CPU-years and leaves the 9-regular case at 40 open.
Searches over 37 million 39-vertex graphs found no extension, so it leans to 'none exists', modestly, because one witness checks in seconds.
models.text:
RANGE: 0.5%–10%  
POINT: 3%  
DIRECTION: If the lane decides by 30 June 2027, I give about 60% to “none exists” and 40% to a construction.

BASIS: Goedgebeur–Radziszowski reached ≤42 in 2013. Angeltveit reached ≤41 about a decade later, using three CPU-years and a parity argument that leaves the 9-regular case open at 40 vertices. [Angeltveit’s paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.00392v2)  
The lane certified all 977,008 configurations in the regular codegree-seven case with both LRAT checkers. That gives me confidence it can certify a sufficiently small reduction.  
The harder cases set my deadline estimate. None of ten benchmark boards closed within two CPU-hours each. A follow-up spent 13.9 core-hours on one board and still had 242 open leaves.  
Even after two programs excluded 283 of 519 nonregular degree distributions, 236 remained. A proof must also cover asymmetric regular graphs.  
I favor nonexistence because earlier searches failed to extend over 37 million 39-vertex graphs. My conditional lean is modest because a single witness takes seconds to certify. [Goedgebeur–Radziszowski’s extension search](https://www.cs.rit.edu/~spr/PUBL/ber12.pdf)

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: I’d raise the estimate if a structural lemma covered asymmetric graphs and timed certificate replays on the hardest remaining cases put the full run within the pod budget.  
I’d also raise it if a new construction method recovered known Ramsey graphs from scratch and repeatedly produced 40-vertex triangle-free graphs with only one independent 10-set.

This is a model’s forecast, not a commitment.

models.text:
Thu Nov 26 01:35:44 UTC 2026

This is a model's forecast (Claude Opus 5.5), not a commitment.

RANGE: 2%–20%
POINT: 8%
BASIS:
- What is left is exactly (3,10;40), between Exoo's 40 (1989) and Angeltveit's ≤ 41 (EJC 2025). Angeltveit's ≤ 41 took about 3 CPU-years of gluing. The 40-vertex case runs into the near-9-regular slice: for a 9-regular graph every G−N[v] is a (3,9;30,99)-graph, a class estimated at about 10^18 graphs. That class is far larger than anything glued so far.
- A construction is unlikely. Decades of searches (Exoo, McKay, AlphaEvolve in 2026) stop at 39 vertices, and the heuristic consensus leans towards R(3,10) = 40. I put a construction by mid-2027 at about 1%.
- The field is active in 2026: Daugherty–Ward–Ryan, Chen (MTF, δ ≥ 6, 545 degree sequences), McCrea, Pandey–Ravi, Unsolved Lab, and SAT+CAS work (SMS, Li–Duggan–Bright–Ganesh). This makes a non-existence proof plausible within a few years. But the steps so far exclude corners (degree 4, degree 7 with e = 104), not the bulk of the degree-9 window.
- Seven months is short for a new decomposition plus about 10^2–10^3 core-years of checkable certificates. Lifting this would take a well-resourced group (a Heule-type SAT team or an AI lab with compute) that has not yet surfaced, so I add a few percent for that. The question also counts unrefereed public certificates, which widens the target somewhat.

A construction would be quick to verify, but AlphaEvolve reached the same 39 vertices Exoo reached in 1989.
